title: Definition of 'consumer'
summary: A consumer is a person who buys goods or hires/avails services for personal use, for a consideration paid (or promised), and not for resale or commercial purpose.
note: Resale / commercial purpose takes you outside the Act (Sec 2(7) proviso). Confirm the section number on India Code before going live.

title: Consumer rights
summary: Lists the six consumer rights: protection against marketing of goods/services hazardous to life and safety; information on quality, quantity, potency, purity, standard and price; access to a variety of goods at competitive prices; being heard; redressal against unfair trade practices; and consumer education.
note: This is the section to name when the seller never disclosed a material defect or price.

title: Definition of 'defect'
summary: 'Defect' means any fault, imperfection or shortcoming in the quality, potency, quantity, purity, standard or specification of goods which is required to be maintained by law or under a contract.
note: Use for physical goods: dead-on-arrival phone, faulty vehicle, contaminated food.

title: Definition of 'deficiency'
summary: 'Deficiency' means any fault, imperfection, shortcoming or inadequacy in the quality, nature and manner of performance of a service which is required to be maintained by law or under a contract.
note: Use for services: bank, airline, hospital, telecom, courier, builder.

title: Definition of 'unfair trade practice'
summary: Covers false representation of quality/sponsorship, hoarding or destruction of goods to raise prices, publication of advertisements offering false guarantee, and refusing to accept a returned defective product contrary to a stated promise.
note: Section number for 'unfair trade practice' must be re-checked against India Code (it is in the 2(40)-range of the 2019 Act).

title: Objects and purposes of the consumer protection councils
summary: The Central and State Consumer Protection Councils exist to promote and protect the consumer rights enumerated in the Act; a district-level council can be approached to intervene with a trader informally.
note: Councils are advisory/promotional, not adjudicatory - do not describe them as a court.

title: Establishment of the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA)
summary: CCPA is the regulator that can investigate violations of consumer rights, order recall of unsafe goods, order discontinuation of unfair trade practices and misleading advertisements, and file complaints before the commissions.
note: Consumer complaints about misleading ads can be filed at CCPA's portal; keep the section number verified.

title: Filing a complaint before the District Commission
summary: A consumer (or a recognised consumer association, or the CCPA) may file a complaint in the District Commission where the opposite party resides, or where he carries on business, or where the cause of action arises - including where the complainant resides.
note: 'Cause of action arises' includes the place where the complainant resides - this is what lets you file from your own city. Verify the exact subsection wording.

title: Powers of the District Commission on complaint
summary: On proof of a defect or deficiency, the District Commission can order removal of the defect, replacement with goods free of defect, refund of the price paid, removal of the defect in the services, payment of compensation for loss or injury, withdrawal of hazardous goods from the market, and costs.
note: The old 1986 Act carried these powers in Section 14; the 2019 numbering must be confirmed on India Code before use.

title: Limitation period for filing a consumer complaint
summary: A complaint should be filed within two years from the date on which the cause of action arose; a complaint can be admitted after two years only if the complainant satisfies the commission as to sufficient cause for the delay.
note: Drives the deadline tracker. Old numbering was Sec 24A of the 1986 Act; confirm the 2019 number.

title: Appeal against an order of the District Commission
summary: A person aggrieved by a District Commission order can appeal to the State Commission within 45 days of the order, and the State Commission may entertain a delayed appeal on showing sufficient cause.
note: 45-day appeal clock - drives the deadline tracker. Confirm section number.

title: e-Daakhil: electronic filing and hearing
summary: The Act (as amended) provides for electronic filing of complaints and documents and for proceedings to be conducted in electronic form, which is implemented through the national e-Daakhil portal.
note: e-Daakhil is the real portal for online consumer-complaint filing across most commissions.

title: Mediation
summary: Where a settlement may be reached, the commission refers the parties to mediation; a settlement reached through the mediation cell is recorded as an order and is not appealable.
note: Expect the first hearing to be a mediation attempt - set that expectation in the user-facing steps.

act: Consumer Protection (Jurisdiction of the District Commission and the State Commission) Rules, 2021
title: Pecuniary limits of the District and State Commissions
summary: Complaints up to Rs. 50 lakh go to the District Commission, Rs. 50 lakh to Rs. 2 crore to the State Commission, and above Rs. 2 crore to the National Commission.
note: Use to pick the right forum. Re-check the current limits - they have been revised since 2019 and states notify their own.

title: Due diligence by e-commerce entities
summary: Marketplaces must display country of origin of goods, the return/refund/cancellation and warranty policies, seller identity and contact details, and must not manipulate price or features of goods or services.
note: The anchor provision for online-shopping complaints (counterfeit product, no-return policy, fake discount).

title: Grievance officer: acknowledgement and redressal
summary: E-commerce entities must appoint a grievance officer in India, acknowledge a complaint within 48 hours and redress it within the notified timelines; the nodal contact must be published on the site/app.
note: Escalation step 1 for online disputes: written complaint to the grievance officer, then the consumer commission.

title: Sale of commodity not in standard units / under-weight packing
summary: No person shall sell or distribute any commodity in packaged form unless it bears the prescribed declarations (net quantity, month/year of packing, maximum retail price, importer/packer details) and is as per the standard unit of weight or measure.
note: Wrong weight, hidden MRP, over-billing: complaint to the Legal Metrology department of the state.
